A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMT study despite the changed title and substantial revision. All 17 pages of v1 and 12 pages of v2, including figures, equations and appendices, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral and activation analyses, BERT rank-removal and fine-tuning experiments, and CIFAR-10 lazy-learning experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original Pythia training-checkpoint analyses and perplexity experiments, alongside BERT/Llama activation analyses and retained BERT and CIFAR-10 experiments.

M1.justification: v2 removes the Monte Carlo-calibrated singular-vector KS diagnostic developed in v1 Section 4. It also changes the stated activation calculation from an uncentered second moment to mean-subtracted covariance (v1 Eq. 7; v2 Eq. 6). SVD, maximal overlap and singular-value decile removal remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds WikiText and BookCorpus for activation analysis, with BookCorpus also used for language-model perplexity evaluation. The WiC example and MRPC projection experiment in v1 Appendices C and F disappear. BoolQ fine-tuning and the CIFAR-10 appendix experiments remain.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks the proposed RMT diagnostic against competing diagnostic methods. Full-model and lazy/feature-learning controls remain. The removed covariance-projection study in v1 Appendix F is a separate supplementary test of another reduction mechanism, rather than a competing-method evaluation against the diagnostic.

E3.justification: The per-matrix removal evaluation changes from fine-tuned BERT accuracy to pretrained Pythia perplexity. v2 adds checkpoint comparisons and selected-block analyses, replacing BERT-wide averaged covariance analyses with different model/block settings. Mean subtraction also changes the stated activation preprocessing. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-time spectral/overlap analyses and Pythia/Llama block comparisons. It removes v1's WiC case study, before/after fine-tuning spectral analysis, standalone activation-covariance spectra and covariance-projection experiment. Fine-tuning/removal-order ablations and the CIFAR-10 lazy/frozen-layer studies remain.

E5.justification: v1's Monte Carlo calibration, KS hypothesis tests, p-value reporting and 15-vector p-value averaging are absent from v2. This substantially removes statistical testing from the diagnostic. The retained BERT fine-tuning figure still reports five seeds and displays error bars; no increase in runs is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds checkpoint-dependent overlaps and BookCorpus perplexity results showing the importance of small Pythia Up/Down singular-value directions. v1's per-matrix BERT/BoolQ accuracy-drop results, WiC case and MRPC projection results disappear. These involve different settings, not same-setting performance gains. The BERT fine-tuning-order curves and CIFAR-10 results are retained.

T1.justification: The covariance definition changes substantively through mean subtraction. v2 also removes v1's Gaussian singular-vector/KS formalism and Appendix B's regularization-decay derivation. The SVD, Marchenko-Pastur law, maximal-overlap definition and lazy-learning loss remain; no new theorem or proof replaces the removed material.

C1.justification: The central RMT feature-localization and fine-tuning/alignment claims remain. v2 explicitly adds a contribution about when and where small singular values become influential during pretraining, extending v1's conclusion, which emphasized their importance arising during fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving rectangular-matrix reweighting, gradient strength across blocks, GLU-related redundancy and temporal redistribution of information. It removes v1's BoolQ/WiC task-dependence discussion and positional-encoding interpretation of covariance outliers. The warning that apparently random weights can remain functionally important survives in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v2 adds the Pythia-410m-deduped identifier and checkpoint conventions, and changes the cited Zenodo archive from record 13861699 to 14764226. It removes v1's reproducibility statement explaining pre-saved data, notebooks and SLURM workflows. Both versions still state that figure-generation code is available.

R1.justification: v2 adds Papyan and Guth to related work and references supporting Pythia, Llama 3, BoolQ, WikiText and BookCorpus, while dropping the GLUE/SuperGLUE references. The positioning of RMT as a diagnostic and the discussion reconciling Hsu and Sharma remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively rewritten, with standardized matrix terminology and a new architecture/notation section. The singular-vector section is removed, the appendix narrative is substantially reorganized, and the reproducibility statement is replaced by a different closing structure including an impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout and substantially redesigns the figures through overlaid spectra, inset spectra, temporal panels and perplexity plots. Several displays disappear. The fine-tuning-order figure moves from Figure 8 to Figure 7, and the unchanged CIFAR-10 graphic moves from Figure 9 to Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more direct evidence for training-time development and functional importance of small singular-value directions through checkpoint analyses and pretrained-model perplexity ablations (Figures 5–6). This strengthens v1's largely static and downstream fine-tuning argument. The net gain is limited by removal of the KS diagnostic, WiC/MRPC corroboration and detailed reproduction guidance; the retained fine-tuning result itself is unchanged.
